hx_crop_contours — 2D halcon_ext op

• Data kinds: contour → contour

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "hx_crop_contours", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: crop_contours_xld (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

Usage

Crop contours to the central a×b fraction rectangle (keeping only the points inside).

Of each contour's points, keeps only those within hh in the row direction and within ww in the column direction of the image centre (H/2, W/2), discards contours with not even 1 point left, and returns the rest.

• a → half of the kept height hh = (0.3 + 0.6*a) * H/2 (30% to 90% of the whole).

• b → half of the kept width ww = (0.3 + 0.6*b) * W/2 (30% to 90% of the whole). Even at a=b=1 the outer 5% is dropped.

It only thins out points without splitting, so a contour that leaves the rectangle and comes back has its remaining points joined (a jump). To ignore everything outside the rectangle completely, apply hx_split_contours downstream. The version that specifies margins from the image border is hx_clip_contours; the version with 1 knob for a square window is xg_crop_contours.

Try it in Studio

The program below has been verified to run (same input as the figure). In Studio's help this block becomes buttons that load and run it on the spot.

threshold 0.50 0.50
sk_find_contours 0.50 0.50
hx_crop_contours 0.50 0.50
